risk_if_not_implemented: Without AI Model Pollution, AI and autonomous systems may produce unreliable, biased or unsafe outputs, act outside authorized scope, or expose sensitive data. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Modification / Loss of System Integrity (R-AM-2), AI Output / Decision Integrity Failure (R-AI-1), AI Data Confidentiality / Integrity / Provenance Loss (R-AI-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning (MT-12), Artificial Intelligence & Autonomous Technologies (AAT) System Failure or Unintended Behavior (MT-13), Adversarial Artificial Intelligence (AI) Attack (MT-29).

compensating_control_1.name: Data Backups
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to create recurring backups of data, software and/or system images, as well as verify the integrity of these backups, to ensure the availability of the data to satisfy Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs).
compensating_control_1.justification: Data Backups (BCD-24) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Model Pollution (AAT-38.1) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Alternate Processing Site
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to establish an alternate processing site that provides processing capability and security measures equivalent to that of the primary site.
compensating_control_2.justification: Alternate Processing Site (BCD-13) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Model Pollution (AAT-38.1) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
